user.description: Measure how much CPU time each integration uses on the event loop.

sampler_failed.message: Integration Insights could not start its sampler: {error}

measuring.title: Still measuring
measuring.description: Findings start once Home Assistant has settled after a start, in about {minutes} minutes. The CPU and Memory views already show the numbers.

measuring_incomplete.title: Some measurements were lost
measuring_incomplete.description: The sampler lost samples or ran into errors. The numbers still show who uses the most, but they are less exact.

busy_loop.title: {name} keeps Home Assistant busy
busy_loop.description:
Over the last {minutes} minutes, {name} used the event loop for {ms} ms a minute, {share}% of all CPU time on the event loop. While it runs, everything else waits: automations, the dashboard and other integrations.

What you can do:
- Check whether an update of {name} is available.
- Look for a report, or open one, at [the issue tracker]({issues_url}), and add the report from this page.
- To confirm, [disable {name}]({config_url}) for a while and compare.

busy_thread.title: {name} keeps background threads busy
busy_thread.description:
Over the last {minutes} minutes, threads of {name} used {ms} ms of CPU a minute. They run beside the event loop, but they cost CPU and power, and that adds up on small hardware.

What you can do:
- Check whether an update of {name} is available.
- Look for a report, or open one, at [the issue tracker]({issues_url}), and add the report from this page.

busy_executor.title: {name} keeps handing off work
busy_executor.description:
Over the last {minutes} minutes, {name} ran {jobs} jobs a minute in the background, using {ms} ms of CPU a minute. That many jobs can mean it polls or reads files more often than it needs to.

What you can do:
- Check the options of {name} for an update interval.
- Check whether an update of {name} is available.
- Look for a report, or open one, at [the issue tracker]({issues_url}), and add the report from this page.

loop_waits.title: The event loop often waits
loop_waits.description:
Over the last {minutes} minutes, the event loop was busy {ms} ms a minute longer than it used the CPU. It was waiting: on a blocking call such as reading a file or the network, on a busy thread that held Python's interpreter lock, or for a free CPU core. Home Assistant does nothing else while it waits.

What you can do:
- Look in the log for "Detected blocking call", which names the integration.
- This page measures CPU time, so it cannot tell which integration made the event loop wait.

growing_resources.title: {name} may be leaking
growing_resources.description:
Between the last two memory snapshots {name} added {what} and did not release them. If this keeps growing over hours, memory use rises until Home Assistant restarts.

What you can do:
- Take another snapshot later. If the numbers keep growing, report it at [the issue tracker]({issues_url}) with the report from this page.
- Check whether an update of {name} is available.
